paragraphs: Chiyya: R. Avin bar Chiyya; R. Adda bar Chiyya; Rav Ammi bar Chiyya; Rav Assi bar Chiyya; R. Binyamin bar Chiyya; Rav Chinena bar Chiyya; Rav Yosef bar Chiyya; R. Yitzchak bar Chiyya; Levi bar Chiyya; Minyamin bar Chiyya; Mar bar Chiyya; Mar Ukva bar Chiyya; Rav Anan bar Chiyya; Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya; R. Shimon bar Chiyya; R. Tanchum bar Chiyya. [Glosses: Chiyya. (a) Shabbat 113a: “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya said: R. Yochanan said.” I think this is a scribal error and should read “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Yochanan said.” In the new Talmud editions the reading was changed, and beside it was written: another version, “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Ashi said: Rav said”—so too in Asheri; another version, “R. Chiyya said: R. Yochanan said.” Rif has “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Rav said.” (b) Zevachim 25b: “R. Chiyya [bar Abba] said: R. Yochanan said.” This should be the reading, as appears there; it was not corrected. (c) Ketubot 8b: Rav Chiyya bar Abba taught Scripture to Resh Lakish's son. It seems likely to me that it should read Rav Chiyya bar Adda, since Ketubot 111b, near the end, says that he taught Resh Lakish's young children. (d) Berakhot 42a has Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi, while everywhere else it is Rav Chiyya. (e) Pesachim 7a and Bekhorot 39a have R. Chiyya bar Yosi; likewise Bava Metzia 117a. It should read bar Yosef, but was not corrected. (f) Niddah 45a: R. Chiyya bar Rav Ika. I think this should read Chinena; it was not corrected. (g) Gittin 22a: R. Chiyya bar Assi, in Ulla's name. Perhaps it should read Ammi; it was not corrected. Later I saw that matter in Shabbat in the name of bar Ammi, and was pleased.]
